Repo: /Users/marcel.a.n.navarro/Dev/zimmermann-pwa, branch feature/SFCC-236_product-card-shared-component.

Test Step 5 of the SFCC-236 build: `ZimmProductCardContent` molecule. Files:
- overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent/{index.tsx,index.stories.tsx,index.test.tsx,zimmProductCardContent.css.ts}
- overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts (1 import + 1 registry entry)

## What this component is
The text-content block below the product image on the shared product card: name (as a link to the PDP), a bag button, an attributes row (colour+size, wishlist only), price, a size-chip picker slot (PLP only), and a notify-me button (out-of-stock only). Composes four already-committed pieces: `ZimmProductName`, `ZimmProductPrice` (Step 3), `ZimmSizeChipGroup` (Step 2). Two things were deliberately excluded per explicit instruction and must NOT be present: no badge (removed from the whole card in Step 4 — "no design exists needing a badge in the image, take this out"), no remove/close button (lives entirely in `ZimmProductCardMedia` from Step 4).

## Known pattern this build has already caught TWICE — verify it wasn't missed a third time
Steps 2 and 4 both shipped interactive controls with zero `_focusVisible` styling, caught only by Tester/Scorer mutation testing after the fact. This step's bag button, name-link, and notify-me button all need the same `var(--zimm-focus-ring)` / `var(--zimm-focus-ring-offset-default)` pair every other interactive ui-kits control uses. The Implementer claims this was added proactively this time, with a "real, unmocked recipe" structural test proving it (same technique Step 4's Fix 1 established). Verify this claim directly — read the recipe, don't trust the report — and mutation-test it exactly like Step 4's Fix 1 was mutation-tested (delete/neutralise one of the three `_focusVisible` blocks, confirm the NEW structural test actually catches it, revert, confirm clean).

## Required pass criteria — verify each independently

1. **No badge, anywhere** — grep the whole component for "badge" (case-insensitive). Must be zero hits in this component's own logic (matches in a comment explaining the exclusion are fine and expected).
2. **No remove/close button** — no `onRemove`/`removeLabel` props, no remove-button rendering.
3. **Bag control**: native `<button>`, real `aria-label`, ≥24×24 hit area, uses `ZimmIcon type="bag"` (verify this is the actual registered icon name in `zimmIcon/index.tsx`'s icon map, not a guessed string), `aria-hidden` on the icon itself since the button carries the label. Disabled (native `disabled` attribute) when `isUnavailable`, and `onAddToBag` genuinely never fires when disabled — verify with a real click-while-disabled test, not just presence of the `disabled` attribute.
4. **Attributes row absent from DOM (not just hidden) when `showAttributes=false`** — confirm the test uses `queryBy...` returning `null`, not a style/visibility check.
5. **Attributes row shows `colour`+`size` as visible text when `showAttributes=true`.**
6. **Price always composes `ZimmProductPrice` with `isLive={false}`** — this is the entire point of Step 3's prop. Verify by reading the actual JSX call site (not just a passing test) that `isLive={false}` is hardcoded there, not accidentally omitted (which would silently default to `true`). Also verify price is rendered in EVERY configuration (not conditionally mounted/unmounted based on variation flags) — hover reveal/hide is supposed to be a CSS concern for Step 6, not a conditional-render concern here.
7. **Size-chip slot**: composes the REAL `ZimmSizeChipGroup` (import, not reimplementation) when `showSizeChips=true`; absent entirely when false. Critically: **this component's OWN recipe must NOT set `display:none` on the size-chip wrapper by default** — Figma shows this slot hidden by default on the card, but the plan is explicit that hiding it is Step 6's (the organism's) job via hover-reveal CSS, not this component's. If this component's recipe hides it, Step 6 would have nothing to reveal. Verify this directly by reading the recipe's `sizeChipWrapper`-equivalent part and confirming no `display:none`/`visibility:hidden`/`opacity:0` exists on it in the base style.
8. **Notify-me renders ONLY when `showNotifyMe=true` AND `onNotifyMe` is supplied** — test both conditions independently (one true, one false, in both directions) to confirm it's a genuine AND, not an OR or a single-flag check.
9. **Exactly one heading per card**, composing the real `ZimmProductName` atom (not reimplemented), at the caller's heading level.
10. **Name renders as a real link to the PDP.** The Implementer reports `ZimmProductName` itself renders no anchor, so this component wraps it in `chakra(RouteLink)` from `react-router-dom`, matching `ZimmColourSwatch`'s existing precedent. Verify: (a) this precedent claim is real — read `zimmColourSwatch/index.tsx` and confirm it actually does this; (b) the resulting DOM has exactly one link wrapping the name, not a nested/duplicate anchor structure; (c) `href` is NOT run through `isSafeHref` — the Implementer's justification is that this is an SFCC-generated PDP URL, "the same trust level ZimmColourSwatch's own href already assumes, not CMS content." Verify this reasoning holds by checking what `isSafeHref` actually gates against in this codebase (grep for its usage) and whether an SFCC-internal product URL is genuinely a different trust boundary than CMS-authored content, or whether this is a rationalization for skipping a safety check that should apply universally to any href reaching an anchor tag.
11. **`_focusVisible` on all three interactive controls** (name-link, bag button, notify-me button) — the specific focus this report should have, per the "caught twice already" framing above.
12. **`headingLevel`/`as` prop type**: Implementer reports deviating from the task's sketch (`'h2'|'h3'|'h4'`) to derive the type via `React.ComponentProps<typeof ZimmProductName>['as']` (real atom type is `'h1'|'h2'|'h3'`). Verify this is genuinely correct (no `'h4'` exists on the atom) and that using a derived utility type instead of a hand-typed union is the right call per this codebase's typescript.md conventions — or is this actually removing type safety this component's own callers need (e.g. if a caller who only knows THIS component's contract, not the atom's, would reasonably expect 'h4' to be valid)?
13. **`data-card-slot` values**: Implementer added 3 beyond what was strictly listed (`content`, `price`, `sizeChips`) reportedly to give Step 6 hover-reveal hooks. Verify these are documented in a top-of-file contract comment matching `zimmProductCardMedia`'s established convention, and that they don't collide with any of Step 4's already-established slot names (`media`, `close`, `carousel`, `indicator`).
14. **No responsive media query added** — Implementer reports finding nothing correctness-critical to gate behind a breakpoint. Sanity-check this claim by reading the recipe yourself — is there genuinely no Desktop/Mobile visual difference in the Figma citation (208x82 Desktop Card-content vs the Mobile variant) that would actually need one, or did the Implementer skip something real?

## Falsification requirements
Required minimum, all three:
(a) The `_focusVisible` structural test — mutate one of the three blocks away, confirm the new real-recipe test catches it, revert.
(b) The bag-disabled-never-fires test — mutate `isUnavailable`'s disabled logic away (e.g. remove the `disabled` attribute binding), confirm the existing test catches a click firing `onAddToBag` when it shouldn't, revert.
(c) The size-chip-wrapper-not-hidden claim — this is the most important one structurally, since getting it backwards would silently break Step 6 later. Actually verify by reading the compiled recipe object's `sizeChipWrapper` (or whatever it's actually named) part's `display` value directly — don't just trust a comment saying it's not hidden.

## Commands to run yourself
```
npx tsc --noEmit
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent
npx vitest run overrides/app/components/ui-kits/recipeParts.test.ts
npx vitest run overrides/app/theme/components/recipeGuards.test.ts
npx eslint overrides/app/components/ui-kits/molecules/zimmProductCardContent overrides/app/theme/components/index.ts
node scripts/auditTokenUsage.mjs
npm run test
```
Baseline going into this step: 50 files / 765 tests (confirmed after Step 4's badge removal, committed as c3eff5c). The Implementer claims 51/792 after this step (765 + 26 new + 1 recipeParts growth). Verify this reconciliation holds, don't just accept the number.

Report CONFIRMED/PLAUSIBLE findings, UNIFORM vs ONE-OFF, what you falsified, what you could not verify.

1	/**
2	 * Allow-list guard for hrefs that originate outside the codebase.
3	 *
4	 * Anything reaching an `href` from Contentful, a URL parameter, or a prop supplied by a
5	 * caller we do not control has to pass through here first. `javascript:` and `data:` URLs
6	 * execute; an authority reference like `//host` silently leaves the site. The `(?![/\\])`
7	 * lookahead rejects that, including the backslash form — a browser treats `/\host` as `//host`,
8	 * so a backslash is an authority reference just as much as a second slash is. `e9c2180` closed
9	 * only the forward-slash half; the backslash and control-character forms stayed open until now.
10	 *
11	 * Allow-list rather than deny-list on purpose: a deny-list has to anticipate every scheme,
12	 * and browsers keep adding them.
13	 */
14	// eslint-disable no-control-regex — the control characters ARE the subject here. The rule exists
15	// to catch them appearing by accident; these are deliberate, and matching them is the whole point
16	// of the fix. Suppressed at the point of use rather than in .eslintrc, per the escape-hatch
17	// convention in .claude/rules/typescript.md.
18	/* eslint-disable no-control-regex */
19	const C0_OR_SPACE = /^[\u0000-\u0020]+|[\u0000-\u0020]+$/g;
20	const TAB_LF_CR = /[\u0009\u000a\u000d]/g;
21	/* eslint-enable no-control-regex */
22	
23	/**
24	 * Normalise the way the URL parser will, before testing.
25	 *
26	 * The WHATWG parser strips leading and trailing C0-or-space, and removes tab/LF/CR from anywhere
27	 * in the input, BEFORE it parses. `/\u0009/evil.com` is therefore parsed as `//evil.com`. Testing
28	 * the raw string means the allow-list checks a different value than the browser resolves — which
29	 * is exactly how the earlier fix passed its own tests while leaving the hole open.
30	 *
31	 * A plain space is deliberately not stripped: the parser percent-encodes it rather than removing
32	 * it, so `/ /evil.com` resolves on-site and must stay allowed.
33	 */
34	const normalise = (href: string): string => href.replace(C0_OR_SPACE, '').replace(TAB_LF_CR, '');
35	
36	const SAFE_HREF_RE = /^(https?:|tel:|mailto:|#|\/(?![/\\]))/i;
37	
38	/** True when `href` is safe to render on an anchor. Absent or unsafe values return false. */
39	export const isSafeHref = (href: string | undefined): boolean => (href ? SAFE_HREF_RE.test(normalise(href)) : false);

2	 * Recipe guards — regression tests for four failure modes that reached a feature branch
3	 * despite passing `tsc`, `eslint`, `vitest`, CodeRabbit and the Storybook a11y run.
4	 *
5	 * All four share a shape: the value is a *valid* `SystemStyleObject` entry, so TypeScript is
6	 * satisfied; no lint rule covers it; and nothing asserts layout. Each one renders plausible,
7	 * wrong output that is only visible by opening the page.
8	 *
9	 *   1. A spacing-scale key on a sizing property. Chakra resolves `width`/`height`/`boxSize`
10	 *      through `theme.sizes`, not `theme.space`. The Zimmermann named scale is registered as
11	 *      `space` only (deliberately — see foundation/sizes.ts), so `width: 'xl'` silently reads
12	 *      Chakra's default `sizes.xl` = 36rem. It shipped a 576px icon and collapsed the footer.
13	 *
14	 *   2. The same trap on a typography property. `fontSizes`/`lineHeights`/`letterSpacings` are
15	 *      deliberately NOT registered either (theme/index.ts explains why), so a bare key reads
16	 *      Chakra's default or resolves to nothing at all. See TYPOGRAPHY_PROPS below.
17	 *
18	 *   3. A recipe key that collides with a base SFCC recipe. `theme/index.ts` composes with
19	 *      `extendTheme(baseTheme, overrides)`, which DEEP MERGES — a recipe named `Footer` does
20	 *      not replace SFCC's `Footer`, it inherits it. Shared part names then pick up base
21	 *      properties, and a key you add that the base lacks is appended last, so a CSS shorthand
